## 1. What was read

**948 research articles** from 32 of the 33 journals on the roster, filtered to `journal article` and excluding reviews, editorials, news, comment and case reports.

| General | Cancer | Immune | Bioinfo | Sysbio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 484 | 139 | 77 | 226 | 22 |

!!! warning "Volume swing against the median month: cancer -28%"
    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months — queried directly, PubMed returns zero *Nucleic Acids Research* research articles dated 2025-12, and zero *Bioinformatics* in 2024-04, 2025-01, 2025-04 and 2026-03. Those holes are in the source and are reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest, so a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: Nature 114, Science 89, JAMA 82, Nucleic Acids Res 77, Bioinformatics 60, Cell 49.

## 3. The evidence that moved it

**The vaccine thread's best clinical evidence is from February 2024.**
[38246194](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38246194/) (*Lancet*) is KEYNOTE-942: individualised neoantigen therapy
mRNA-4157 plus pembrolizumab versus pembrolizumab alone in resected melanoma,
randomised. Nothing later in this corpus supports the neoantigen thread as
strongly, and by 2026-07 the same thread is being attacked on both its target
space and its selection method. The high-water mark is at the start.

**CAR-T's secondary-malignancy problem reaches NEJM in one month.**
[38265704](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38265704/): secondary cancers after CAR-T. [38195751](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38195751/) (*Nat Med*):
unanswered questions following those reports. [38206604](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38206604/) carries the safety
notice in *JAMA*. January's regulatory signal becomes February's flagship
clinical literature — a four-week lag, which is the fastest this corpus records
for anything.

**And the indication that saves the platform is already in NEJM.**
[38381673](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38381673/): CD19 CAR-T in autoimmune disease, a case series with follow-up.
The corpus's November 2025 briefing calls autoimmunity CAR-T's growth edge and
treats it as a recent turn. It is in the flagship clinical journal in February
2024.

**ctDNA converges on residual disease.** [37972346](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37972346/) clinically validates
HPV ctDNA for residual disease after chemoradiation in cervical cancer;
[37992871](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37992871/) uses ctDNA and radiological volume to identify relapse risk in
resected NSCLC; [38361060](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38361060/) attacks the sensitivity floor at the assay
level. Detection is being solved here. What fails in 2026 is not detection but
the intervention triggered by it.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

The CAR-T items above are refutations on `cell-therapy` and are filed as such.
They are worth reading against the same month's [38316518](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38316518/), a complete
response in gastric cancer from Claudin18.2 CAR-T — the target that in June 2026
becomes the first CAR-T approved anywhere for a solid tumour. Both the platform's
liability and its eventual solid-tumour success are visible in the same month.

### (b) Method credibility

[38200587](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38200587/) (*Bioinformatics*): pitfalls of machine learning models for
protein-protein interaction networks. This is the direct ancestor of the July
2025 finding that sequence-based interaction predictors plateau at 0.65 — the
same objection, seventeen months earlier, in the same journal.

[38331411](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38331411/): *zero is not absence*. The standard handling of zeros in
microbiome differential-abundance testing is wrong and censoring-based analysis
is required. [38279041](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38279041/) (*Nat Genet*): adjusting for genetic confounders in
transcriptome-wide association studies improves discovery — which says the
unadjusted analyses already in the literature were confounded.
